sentences.text: Guanlingsaurus was an extinct shastasaurid ichthyosaur that lived in China during the Late Triassic period.
This creature reached a maximum length of 8.3 meters and featured a wide, triangular skull with a short, toothless snout.
The very short snout was highly compressed through a unique arrangement of skull bones.
Both adult and juvenile Guanlingsaurus specimens completely lacked teeth and did not possess a dental groove.
Some sources state that Guanlingsaurus grew to approximately 10 meters in length.
Guanlingsaurus was first named in 2000 based on an incomplete adult skeleton.
More complete skeletons were described in 2011, and a complete juvenile skeleton was described in 2013.
Typicusichthyosaurus tsaihuae was proposed as a synonym for Guanlingsaurus in 2000.
Guanlingsaurus is classified within the family Shastasauridae.
Fossil evidence dates Guanlingsaurus to the Carnian age, between 237 and 227.3 million years ago.
